newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Gazprom decries Czech gas deal as threat.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Gazprom decries Czech gas deal as threat.

text.p: Russia's natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom lashed out on Friday at the Czech Republic's landmark deal to buy Norwegian gas, saying similar moves by other clients could hurt Gazprom's competitive position in Europe.
A Gazprom press release said that the Russian monopoly considered Prague's decision incorrect and economically unjustified.
"Similar decisions would undoubtedly affect Gazprom's inherent interests in European gas markets," it said.
"Gazprom cannot agree with the assessment of (Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir) Dlouhy that the higher cost of Norwegian gas is offset by its more reliable supply."
The Czech Republic signed a key 20-year deal on Wednesday to end more than 50 years of total dependence on Gazprom for natural gas by contracting for supplies from Russian gas competitor Norway.

Under the deal, Norwegian supplies would increase from 1.4 million cubic metres a day from May 1 to around three billion cubic metres annually. Total deliveries under the agreement would be 53 billion cubic metres (bcm).
"The reliability of Russian natural gas supplies to the Czech Republic are supported by a 30-year history," Gazprom said.

"It is this reliability that gives Gazprom's competitors the ability to conclude 20-year contracts which envision the practice of substituting Russian gas and of supplying Russian gas which is then called Norwegian."
Czech annual domestic gas use is around nine bcm, all currently supplied by Russia, but will rise to 12 to 13 bcm after 2000.
Gazprom is still expected to remain a main supplier to the Czechs, but the new deal makes Norway a major and direct competitor to the Russian giant.

"Gazprom is closely following the development of events in the Czech Republic, and remaining its fundamental partner in the field of gas supplies, will do everything possible to widen co-operation," Gazprom said.
Prague said it picked Norway after considering potential deals with German, Dutch and British suppliers, as well as a second delivery route of Russian gas.
